bare_or_subscript_iota_lines.text: 4.2 For $r$ connected boundary tensor objects $X_q$ choose unit-channel composition-dual bases $x_{q,a},y_q^a$. Define $\iota(\bigotimes_qx_q)=\bigotimes_qx_q$ from $\bigotimes_q\operatorname{Hom}(\mathbf1,X_q)$ to $\operatorname{Hom}(\mathbf1,\bigotimes_qX_q)$, and define $\pi(z)=\sum_{a_1,\ldots,a_r}(\bigotimes_qx_{q,a_q})[(\bigotimes_qy_q^{a_q})z]$. Kronecker contraction gives $\pi\iota=1$, while $\iota\pi(z)=(P_{X_1}\otimes\cdots\otimes P_{X_r})z=D^{-2r}(E_{X_1}\otimes\cdots\otimes E_{X_r})z$. These maps are independent of the chosen unit bases because their object-level projectors are. For a special graph with disconnected input/output set $F_0=\pi_{\rm out}\operatorname{Hom}(\mathbf1,F)\iota_{\rm in}$ before the finite surgery-color sum. This retains precisely the required tensor-product channels; the larger Hom of the object tensor product is not silently identified with that tensor product of Hom spaces. [F1, F2, step 3.1, algebra]

7.1 Use the all-$r$ graph, with $m^+=m_1+m_2+G+r$. step 4.2 says its meridian sum inserts $D^{2r}$ times exactly the necessary $\iota\pi$ between the two exterior maps. Thus $F_0(\Omega^+)^l_i=D^{2r}\sum_jd(j)F_0(\Omega_2)^l_jF_0(\Omega_1)^j_i$. The closed connected-sum rule is $\tau(N\#P)=D\tau(N)\tau(P)$: place the two surgery links in disjoint balls; their component counts and signatures add, while the product normalization has one additional $D^{-1}$. The same argument holds for external cap graphs away from the sum balls. Since $\tau(S^1\times S^2)=1$, the extra factor is $D$ and must be divided out. The resulting $D$ exponent is $-m_1-m_2-G-r-2+\chi_{\rm out}/2+2r=-m_1-m_2-G+r-2+\chi_{\rm out}/2$. The product coefficients give exactly the same exponent because $\chi_{\rm middle}/2=r-G$. Every $d(j),d(l)$ also matches. The redundant final zero-framed trace component has signature0, so the actual signatures yield the same discrepancy $\kappa^{\sigma_1+\sigma_2-\sigma}$. [F1, step 3.1, step 4.2, step 6.1, step 6.2, algebra]
